clue.text: Isn't he going to work initially, second to first, at ancient town

indicators.note: first tells us the pieces just named, second and to, come at the front of the answer

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second, as in units of time
taken as written
a question meaning 'won't he?', contracted to WON'T HE with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: ancient means old

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is ever going to start work, in a jumble about an old place.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is deliberately nonsensical. 'First' is a placing instruction: the abbreviation for second and the word to go at the front, ahead of the contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Stow-on-the-Wold is a small market town in the Cotswolds, Gloucestershire, England.

clue.text: 450-inch surround for round object at bottom of ring

indicators.note: surround for means the 450-inch measure is placed around the next piece

parts.note: an ell is an old cloth measure of 45 inches, so ten ells make 450 inches
an orb is a sphere, something round

explanation.surface: A measurement instruction for fitting a hoop around a ball at the base of a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests jewellery or boxing, but it is a set of church bells; the ten ells are split so the sphere sits between them.
explanation.definitionFit: In bell-ringing the tenor is the heaviest, lowest-pitched bell of a ring, sounding at the bottom of the scale.

clue.text: Official publication of 12 11

definitions.meaning: a government document setting out policy proposals
the French phrase at 12 and 11 translates word by word as ... card or ...

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference reads 12-across and 11-across together, a French phrase whose literal English is this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A government report stating policy is known in Britain by this name, from its plain covers; it is also a literal translation of the French phrase.

clue.text: Method not given? On the contrary

definitions.text: Method not given? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary swaps the order of the clue's two words, so the negation comes first

parts.note: no is a word of negation, standing for not
how means the method or manner of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone complains that no method was given, then reverses the complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Method not' read in reverse order gives NO HOW, and saying there is no method describes the word itself, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect or humorous adverb means in no way at all, that is, without any means or method.

clue.text: Without a birthday, year 1 produces a cross condition

indicators.note: produces signals that the remaining letters are worked into a new arrangement
without tells us to drop the article a from the word birthday

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A strange recipe in which removing a birthday and adding a year results in someone being cross.
explanation.walkthrough: BIRTHDAY loses its A, and with Y and I the nine letters are rearranged. 'Cross' looks like anger but means a hybrid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a cross between two species or varieties is the state of a hybrid, so the noun names that condition.

clue.text: What's eating far right movement? They frequent the waterside

indicators.note: eating means the outer word swallows the other letters

parts.note: taken as written, with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: movement signals that the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what is consuming the far-right political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far right movement' reads as politics, but 'movement' rearranges the far and right letters to RFRA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are idlers or petty thieves who hang about docks, as well as the rodents living near wharves.

clue.text: I work with string, shedding some tears

indicators.note: shedding some means a few letters are cast off from the end of that word

parts.note: to lacerate is to tear, so tears gives the verb form ending in -ates

explanation.surface: A craftsman who works with string is moved to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb for 'tears' loses its last four letters, ATES.
explanation.definitionFit: One who threads laces through shoes or garments works with string or cord.

clue.text: The body/mind relationship in film: the film is different without love

parts.note: Psycho is the 1960 Hitchcock thriller

indicators.note: different tells us the remaining letters are put into another order
without means the letter for love is removed from the film's title

parts.note: the same Hitchcock film named again
love is zero in tennis scoring, written O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film critic notes that a movie about body and mind is different without its romance.
explanation.walkthrough: PSYCHO comes first; then PSYCH (PSYCHO without O) plus IS is rearranged to PHYSICS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the branch of psychology studying how physical stimuli relate to mental sensations and perceptions.

clue.text: They prevail in the Guardian way, almost too soon to get document signed

parts.note: the newspaper speaking of itself uses the editorial we
ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: almost means the word for too soon is short of a letter

parts.note: early can mean before the appointed time
to get is to win
DS is a legal abbreviation for document signed

explanation.surface: The newspaper reports it nearly signed a document too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' here removes an inner letter, the A, from EARLY rather than the last one. The setter's newspaper, the Guardian, is WE.
explanation.definitionFit: In temperate latitudes the winds from the west are the prevailing winds, blowing most often.

clue.text: Number embraced by mystic don't sing bass

indicators.note: embraced by means the number is held within the mystic

parts.note: a Sufi is a Muslim mystic
sh is a call for silence, telling someone not to sing

explanation.surface: A mystic tells a bass singer to stop singing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bass' looks like a singer but is the fish; black bass belong to the sunfish family.
explanation.definitionFit: The black bass of North America is one of the freshwater sunfishes, so a bass is an example.

clue.text: See 12
Hiding place includes barn let out — you can do what you like with it

definitions.text: you can do what you like with it

indicators.note: includes means the hiding place holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cache is a hidden store

indicators.note: out signals the letters are released into a new order

explanation.surface: A hiding place in which a barn has been let to tenants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let out' reads as renting, but 'out' rearranges barn and let to RTEBLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means full freedom or discretion, a free hand to act as one wishes.

clue.text: Caroller about to be punished? Don't jump the gun!

parts.note: a wait is one of a band of street carol singers at Christmas
to be for it is to be in line for punishment

explanation.surface: A carol singer is in trouble, and someone urges patience.
explanation.walkthrough: WAITS were the old British bands of Christmas street singers.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation urges patience, telling someone not to start before the right moment arrives.

clue.text: See 19
Every other change involved a 10

parts.note: to alter is to change

indicators.note: involved signals that the letters are tangled into a new order

parts.note: 10 is written out as ten

explanation.surface: A change that involved the number ten, applied every other time.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a cross-reference to 10-across but is just the number. A plus TEN is rearranged to NATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Occurring on every second one, as in alternate days, means taking each other one in turn.

clue.text: Royal couple are flirting

parts.note: the late Queen's husband was Prince Philip, shortened to Phil
the couple are joined by the word and
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen; PHIL is her husband Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to flirt or have casual affairs, so the verb fits a plural subject who are flirting.

clue.text: Fantasy sort of music transmitted by choirs, say

parts.note: piped music is transmitted through speakers
choirs sounds like quires, and a quire is a quantity of paper, as is a ream

explanation.surface: Fantasy music relayed by church choirs.
explanation.walkthrough: Choirs said aloud gives quires, sheets of paper; a ream is twenty quires, so the stationery link gives REAM.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrealistic hope or fanciful scheme is called this, from opium smokers' visions.

clue.text: The luck attached to the tares in the parable?

definitions.meaning: the phrase completes the idiom about exceptional luck, the ___ luck

definitions.text: to the tares in the parable?
definitions.meaning: in the parable of the wheat and the tares the weeds were sown by the enemy, the devil

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as DEVIL SOWN: the tares were sown by the devil in Matthew 13.
explanation.definitionFit: Extraordinary luck is called the devil's own luck, and the parable's weeds were sown by Satan.

clue.text: Trouble meeting 17 demands?

definitions.meaning: serious trouble or punishment to come
the 17-down answer refers to the devil, so meeting his demands would mean paying hell

explanation.walkthrough: 17-down is the devil, so meeting the devil's demands is read as paying hell: a pun on the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means serious trouble or consequences, and literally suggests settling a debt owed to the underworld.

clue.text: Building over a soapy production of 23 down 12

indicators.note: building signals the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A building above a soap opera production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a definition (the Savoy hotel or theatre) but is the anagram signal on OVER A SOAPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic operas were staged by Richard D'Oyly Carte at his Savoy Theatre, hence the name.

clue.text: Settled accounts when prepared to fight

definitions.meaning: took a boxer's stance facing an opponent

explanation.walkthrough: The 'when' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both paid off a debt and adopted a fighting stance against someone.

clue.text: Mythical pope?

definitions.meaning: as in an ... myth, a modern folk tale
eight popes have taken this name

explanation.walkthrough: An urban myth is an untrue modern story, so the adjective stands loosely for mythical.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban was the name of eight popes, and an urban legend is a mythical tale.

clue.text: See 3
Sound food supplier with new capital

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen, a shop supplying food

explanation.surface: A sound grocer opens shop in a new capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Delhi with New before it is India's capital, hence 'with new capital'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian city, given the prefix New, is the national capital of India.

clue.text: 12 could be 22

parts.note: the word before 12-across in the opera company's name, and also a lace mat that could be made of paper

explanation.walkthrough: 12-across with this name before it is the D'Oyly Carte opera company; read alone, the word is a doily, which may be paper (22-down).
explanation.definitionFit: A doily or doyly is a small ornamental mat, often of paper, and D'Oyly Carte named the opera company.

clue.text: A 3 could be 19

parts.note: the 3-down colour and the 19-across name are both varieties of one leafy vegetable

explanation.walkthrough: With 3-down and 19-across in, white and savoy are both kinds of this vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: White cabbage and savoy cabbage are two common varieties of this leafy green vegetable.

clue.text: A lady pilot officer arranged who and what was carried

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters are set in a new order

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for pilot officer, an RAF rank

explanation.surface: A woman pilot organised the passengers and cargo for a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: A LADY plus PO is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the passengers and cargo carried by an aircraft or vehicle, the load that earns revenue.

clue.text: While school is on, lines in a circle are forming union with a close relative or the opposite

definitions.text: forming union with a close relative or the opposite

parts.note: during the school term, in term

indicators.note: in tells us the lines are put inside the circle

parts.note: a ring is a circle
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines

explanation.surface: During term-time, pupils standing in a ring form an alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: RY (railway) goes inside A RING. The word covers marrying within one's family and also marrying across groups.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means marrying within a close family group, or between different races, tribes or groups.
